findings.evidence: Ideal.lean:117-120 `AddSubgroup.closure {f | ∃ S, P S ∧ ∃ V : FDRep k S, indClassFun S V.character = f}` vs Spanning.lean:242-244 `def indCharacterSet … ρ.IsIrreducible ∧ ind S (ofCharacter ρ) = f`; Spanning.lean:375-377 `theorem indVirtualCharacters_eq_indCharacterSpanInt [IsAlgClosed k] (hP : ∀ C, P C → IsUnit (Nat.card C : k))`.
findings.fix: Rename to a token that names the actual generators, e.g. `indVirtualCharacters_eq_closure_indFDRepCharacter`, or give the generating set a def (`indFDRepCharacterSet`) and name the theorem after it.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharacters_eq_closure_indCharacter` names its RHS generators `indCharacter`, but in this development that token already denotes induction of *irreducible* characters (`indCharacterSet`, Spanning.lean:242-244, requires `ρ.IsIrreducible`; `indCharacterSpan`, :256; `indCharacterSpanInt`, :294). The theorem's generators are inductions of characters of arbitrary `FDRep k S`. The name therefore advertises `indVirtualCharacters = closure (indCharacterSet …)` — which is the strictly stronger `indVirtualCharacters_eq_indCharacterSpanInt` (Spanning.lean:375) and needs `[IsAlgClosed k]` plus order invertibility — while this statement is unconditional. `indCharacter` is also not a declaration, breaking the rule that `_`-separated components correspond to a definition name.

findings.evidence: Ideal.lean:238-240 `theorem indVirtualCharacterDirectSumBaseChangeRat_surjective (P) (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) (h : n • (1 : G → k) ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P) : Function.Surjective …`; its own docstring at :236 calls it "a general criterion" and the module docstring at :49 repeats that.
findings.fix: Rename to `indVirtualCharacterDirectSumBaseChangeRat_surjective_of_nsmul_one_mem`, per the `_of_` convention for describing the essential hypothesis.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharacterDirectSumBaseChangeRat_surjective` names an unconditional surjectivity conclusion, but the theorem holds only under `(h : n • (1 : G → k) ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P)` — for e.g. `P = fun _ ↦ False` the map is not surjective. The name is also indistinguishable in form from the genuinely unconditional `indVirtualCharacterDirectSumBaseChangeRat_isCyclic_surjective` (Artin.lean:200) and `_isElementary_surjective` (Artin.lean:230), so the hypothesis that carries all the content is invisible.

summary: Two names overstate or misdescribe their statements: `indVirtualCharacters_eq_closure_indCharacter` reuses the token `indCharacter`, which this development has fixed to mean "induced irreducible character", for a set of inductions of arbitrary FDRep characters, and `indVirtualCharacterDirectSumBaseChangeRat_surjective` names a hypothesis-driven criterion as an unconditional surjectivity theorem. Everything else (natCard_nsmul, _apply_coe, _of, _tmul, the family suffixes) follows existing precedent, and no notation is added.
